questions.subject: C
questions.questionText: The Zoji La Pass connects which two regions?
questions.explanation: Zoji La Pass (3,528 m) lies on the Srinagar-Leh Highway and connects the Kashmir Valley to Ladakh. 'Kashmir Valley and Jammu' is wrong because that connection is through Banihal Pass/Jawahar Tunnel. 'Ladakh and Himachal Pradesh' is wrong as no major pass of that name serves that route. 'Jammu and Ladakh' is wrong because the Jammu-Ladakh route goes via Kashmir first.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText:
Consider the following statements about the Tawi River:

(i) It originates from the Kali Kundi glacier in the Pir Panjal range.
(ii) It flows through the city of Jammu.
(iii) It is a tributary of the Jhelum River.
(iv) The Bahu Fort is situated on its left bank.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: The Tawi originates from the Kali Kundi glacier in Pir Panjal (i-correct), flows through Jammu city (ii-correct), and the Bahu Fort sits on its left bank (iv-correct). Statement (iii) is wrong because the Tawi is a tributary of the Chenab, not the Jhelum. Option '(i), (ii) and (iii)' wrongly includes the Jhelum connection. Option '(ii), (iii) and (iv)' wrongly includes (iii) and omits (i). Option '(i), (iii) and (iv)' wrongly includes (iii) and omits (ii).

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText: The Mubarak Mandi Palace complex in Jammu was primarily used as the royal residence of which ruling dynasty?
questions.explanation: Mubarak Mandi was the principal royal residence of the Dogra rulers of Jammu & Kashmir from the mid-19th century. 'Mughal dynasty' is wrong because Mughals built gardens in Kashmir, not palaces in Jammu. 'Sikh rulers' is wrong because Sikh rule ended in 1846 and they did not build this complex. 'Afghan governors' is wrong because Afghan rule ended in 1819 and they had no such palace in Jammu.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText:
Given below are two statements, one labeled as Assertion (A) and the other as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): The Karewa deposits in the Kashmir Valley are ideal for saffron cultivation.
Reason (R): Karewas are elevated plateaus of lacustrine deposits with well-drained loamy soil that suits the crocus plant.

Choose the correct option:
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
questions.correctAnswer: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
questions.explanation: Karewas are indeed suitable for saffron (A is correct). Their elevated, well-drained loamy composition directly explains why saffron thrives there (R is correct and explains A). Option 'Both correct but R is NOT the explanation' is wrong because the drainage and soil properties directly cause saffron suitability. Option 'A correct but R not correct' is wrong because R accurately describes Karewas. Option 'A not correct but R correct' is wrong because A is a well-established fact.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText:
Which of the following are correctly matched (district — its division)?

(i) Rajouri — Jammu Division
(ii) Shopian — Kashmir Division
(iii) Kishtwar — Kashmir Division
(iv) Ganderbal — Kashmir Division

Select the correct combination:
questions.explanation: Rajouri is in Jammu Division (i-correct), Shopian is in Kashmir Division (ii-correct), and Ganderbal is in Kashmir Division (iv-correct). Kishtwar belongs to Jammu Division, not Kashmir (iii-wrong). Option '(i), (ii) and (iii)' wrongly includes Kishtwar in Kashmir. Option '(ii), (iii) and (iv)' wrongly includes (iii) and omits (i). Option '(i), (iii) and (iv)' wrongly includes (iii) and omits (ii).

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText:
Match the following rivers with their ancient Sanskrit names:

Column I:
(a) Jhelum
(b) Chenab
(c) Ravi
(d) Indus

Column II:
(i) Sindhu
(ii) Vitasta
(iii) Asikni
(iv) Purushni

Choose the correct match:
questions.explanation: Jhelum = Vitasta (ii), Chenab = Asikni (iii), Ravi = Purushni (iv), Indus = Sindhu (i). Option '(a)-(iii)...' wrongly assigns Asikni to Jhelum. Option '(a)-(ii), (b)-(iv)...' wrongly assigns Purushni to Chenab. Option '(a)-(i)...' wrongly assigns Sindhu to Jhelum.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText: The 'Naya Kashmir' manifesto was drafted in 1944 under whose leadership?
questions.explanation: The Naya Kashmir manifesto (1944) outlined a vision for a progressive, democratic Kashmir and was drafted under Sheikh Abdullah's leadership in the National Conference. 'Bakshi Ghulam Mohammad' is wrong as he succeeded Sheikh Abdullah later as PM. 'Maharaja Hari Singh' is wrong as it was an opposition document against princely rule. 'Ghulam Mohammad Sadiq' is wrong; he became Chief Minister much later in the 1960s.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText:
Consider the following statements about the Mughal Road in J&K:

(i) It connects Shopian in Kashmir to Rajouri-Poonch in Jammu.
(ii) It was built by Emperor Akbar as an alternate route to Kashmir.
(iii) It crosses the Pir Panjal range.
(iv) It is also known as the National Highway 44.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: The Mughal Road connects Shopian to Rajouri/Poonch (i-correct), was originally built by Akbar as an alternate route to Kashmir (ii-correct), and crosses the Pir Panjal range (iii-correct). Statement (iv) is wrong because NH-44 is the Jammu-Srinagar highway via Banihal, not the Mughal Road. Option '(i), (iii) and (iv)' wrongly includes (iv). Option '(ii), (iii) and (iv)' wrongly includes (iv) and omits (i). Option '(i), (ii) and (iv)' wrongly includes (iv) and omits (iii).

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText: The Lidder River originates from which glacier in J&K?
questions.explanation: The Lidder River originates from the Kolahoi Glacier in the Anantnag district. 'Machoi Glacier' is wrong as it is the source of the Sind (Sindh) River near Sonamarg. 'Thajiwas Glacier' is wrong; it is near Sonamarg and feeds into the Sind. 'Siachen Glacier' is wrong as it is in Ladakh and feeds the Nubra River system.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText:
Given below are two statements, one labeled as Assertion (A) and the other as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): The Pashmina shawl of Kashmir has received a Geographical Indication (GI) tag.
Reason (R): Pashmina is made from the fine cashmere wool of the Changthangi goat found in Ladakh.

Choose the correct option:
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
questions.correctAnswer: Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A)
questions.explanation: Kashmir Pashmina does have a GI tag (A-correct), and it is indeed made from Changthangi goat wool from Ladakh (R-correct). However, the GI tag was granted because of the unique hand-spinning and hand-weaving craft tradition of Kashmir artisans, not merely because of the raw material source. So R does not explain why the GI was awarded. Option 'R is the correct explanation' is wrong because GI relates to the craftsmanship, not just material origin. Option 'A correct, R not correct' is wrong because R is factually accurate. Option 'A not correct but R correct' is wrong because A is factual.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText: What does the abbreviation 'JKEDI' stand for?
questions.explanation: JKEDI stands for Jammu & Kashmir Entrepreneurship Development Institute, which promotes self-employment and enterprise. 'Economic Development Initiative' is wrong; no such body exists by that name. 'Educational Development Institute' is wrong as JKEDI focuses on entrepreneurship, not education. 'Employment Development Initiative' is wrong; the correct word is Entrepreneurship.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText: The Hemis National Park in Ladakh is primarily known for the conservation of which endangered species?
questions.explanation: Hemis National Park in Ladakh is the premier habitat and conservation area for the Snow Leopard. 'Hangul (Kashmir Stag)' is wrong because Hangul is conserved in Dachigam National Park. 'Himalayan Brown Bear' is wrong; while present in some areas, Hemis is not primarily known for it. 'Tibetan Wild Ass' (Kiang) is wrong as it is found in Changthang but not in Hemis specifically.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText:
Consider the following statements about the J&K Bank:

(i) It was established in 1938.
(ii) It was founded by Maharaja Hari Singh.
(iii) It functions as the banker to the government of UT of J&K.
(iv) Its headquarters are in Srinagar.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: J&K Bank was established in 1938 (i-correct), functions as banker to the UT government (iii-correct), and has its HQ in Srinagar (iv-correct). Statement (ii) is incorrect — it was not founded by Maharaja Hari Singh personally; it was incorporated as a banking company under the Companies Act. Option '(i), (ii) and (iii)' wrongly includes (ii) and omits (iv). Option '(ii), (iii) and (iv)' wrongly includes (ii) and omits (i). Option 'All of the above' wrongly includes (ii).

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText:
Match the following districts with their famous products/features:

Column I:
(a) Budgam
(b) Kathua
(c) Kulgam
(d) Doda

Column II:
(i) Basmati rice cultivation
(ii) Aharbal Waterfall
(iii) Lavender cultivation (Purple Revolution)
(iv) Yusmarg hill station

Choose the correct match:
questions.explanation: Budgam is known for Yusmarg (iv), Kathua for Basmati rice (i), Kulgam for Aharbal Waterfall (ii), and Doda for lavender/Purple Revolution (iii). Option '(a)-(iii)...' wrongly assigns lavender to Budgam. Option '(a)-(iv), (b)-(iii)...' wrongly assigns lavender to Kathua. Option '(a)-(ii)...' wrongly assigns Aharbal to Budgam.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText: The 'Wazwan' in Kashmiri culture refers to:
options: A multi-course feast served at celebrations and weddings
A traditional wooden houseboats on Dal Lake
An ancient Kashmiri martial art form
A type of traditional Kashmiri embroidery pattern
questions.correctAnswer: A multi-course feast served at celebrations and weddings
questions.explanation: Wazwan is the elaborate multi-course meal (up to 36 courses) that forms the centrepiece of Kashmiri celebrations, especially weddings. 'Traditional wooden houseboats' is wrong; houseboats are called 'Doongas'. 'Ancient Kashmiri martial art' is wrong; no such association exists. 'Traditional embroidery pattern' is wrong; Kashmiri embroidery is called 'Aari' or 'Sozni'.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText:
Given below are two statements, one labeled as Assertion (A) and the other as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): The Chenani-Nashri Tunnel significantly reduced travel time on the Jammu-Srinagar highway.
Reason (R): The tunnel bypasses the Patnitop-Ramban section which was prone to landslides and snowfall.

Choose the correct option:
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
questions.correctAnswer: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
questions.explanation: The tunnel reduced travel time by about 2 hours (A-correct), and this is because it bypasses the landslide/snowfall-prone stretch (R-correct and explains A). Option 'R is NOT the explanation' is wrong because bypassing the difficult terrain is exactly why travel time reduced. Option 'A correct, R not correct' is wrong because R accurately describes the terrain issues. Option 'A not correct' is wrong because the time reduction is well-documented.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText: The famous Shikara boats of Kashmir are traditionally made from which type of wood?
questions.explanation: Shikaras are traditionally built using Deodar (Cedrus deodara) wood, prized for its water resistance and durability. 'Walnut wood' is wrong; walnut is used for carved furniture and handicrafts. 'Willow wood' is wrong; it is used for cricket bats. 'Chinar wood' is wrong; Chinar trees are ornamental and protected, not used for boat-building.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText:
Consider the following statements about the Dogra period in J&K:

(i) Maharaja Gulab Singh was the first Dogra ruler of J&K.
(ii) Maharaja Pratap Singh introduced the State Subject Law in 1927.
(iii) Maharaja Ranbir Singh established the Raghunath Temple in Jammu.
(iv) The Dogra dynasty ruled J&K for exactly 101 years.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: Gulab Singh was the first Dogra ruler (i-correct), Ranbir Singh completed and established the Raghunath Temple (iii-correct), and the dynasty ruled from 1846 to 1947 = 101 years (iv-correct). Statement (ii) is wrong because the State Subject (Hereditary State Subject) law was introduced by Maharaja Hari Singh in 1927, not Pratap Singh. Option '(i), (ii) and (iii)' wrongly includes (ii). Option '(ii), (iii) and (iv)' wrongly includes (ii) and omits (i). Option '(i), (ii) and (iv)' wrongly includes (ii) and omits (iii).

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText:
Which of the following are tributaries of the Chenab River in J&K?

(i) Tawi
(ii) Marusudar
(iii) Sind (Sindh)
(iv) Ans

Select the correct combination:
questions.explanation: Tawi (i), Marusudar (ii), and Ans (iv) are all tributaries of the Chenab. The Sind/Sindh River (iii) is a tributary of the Jhelum, not Chenab. Option '(i), (ii) and (iii)' wrongly includes Sind. Option '(ii), (iii) and (iv)' wrongly includes Sind and omits Tawi. Option '(i), (iii) and (iv)' wrongly includes Sind and omits Marusudar.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText: The Patnitop hill station is located in which district of J&K?
questions.explanation: Patnitop is located in Ramban district (earlier part of Udhampur before the district was reorganized). 'Udhampur' is a common confusion since Patnitop was historically in old Udhampur tehsil, but after reorganization it falls in Ramban. 'Doda' is wrong as Doda is further north. 'Reasi' is wrong as Reasi is south of Ramban.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText:
Match the following lakes of J&K with their types:

Column I:
(a) Wular Lake
(b) Pangong Tso
(c) Sheshnag Lake
(d) Tso Kar

Column II:
(i) Glacial lake
(ii) Freshwater tectonic lake
(iii) Brackish/saline lake
(iv) High-altitude salt lake

Choose the correct match:
questions.explanation: Wular is a freshwater tectonic lake (ii), Pangong Tso is brackish/saline (iii), Sheshnag is a glacial lake (i), and Tso Kar is a high-altitude salt lake (iv). Option '(a)-(iii)...' wrongly calls Wular saline. Option '(a)-(ii), (b)-(i)...' wrongly calls Pangong glacial. Option '(a)-(i)...' wrongly calls Wular glacial.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText: The Lal Ded (Lalleshwari) of 14th century Kashmir is primarily remembered as:
options: A mystic poetess who composed vakhs (verses) promoting spiritual unity
The first woman ruler who established democratic governance
A military leader who resisted Mughal invasion of Kashmir
A scholar who translated the Rajatarangini into Persian
questions.correctAnswer: A mystic poetess who composed vakhs (verses) promoting spiritual unity
questions.explanation: Lal Ded (c. 1320–1392) was a Kashmiri mystic poetess of the Shaivite tradition whose vakhs (verses) preached spiritual devotion and unity. 'First woman ruler' is wrong — Didda was the first woman ruler of Kashmir. 'Military leader against Mughals' is wrong — she lived before the Mughal period. 'Translator of Rajatarangini' is wrong — no such translation is attributed to her.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText: Fill in the blank: The total number of districts in the Union Territory of Jammu & Kashmir (as of 2024) is __________.
questions.explanation: The UT of J&K has 20 districts (10 in Jammu division and 10 in Kashmir division). '22' is wrong as that includes Ladakh's districts. '18' is an older count before recent bifurcations. '24' is incorrect and exceeds the actual number.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText: The Ranbir Canal, one of the oldest irrigation canals of J&K, draws water from which river?
questions.explanation: The Ranbir Canal (built during Maharaja Ranbir Singh's era) draws water from the Chenab river to irrigate the Jammu plains. 'Tawi' is wrong; the Tawi is too small for a major canal system. 'Jhelum' is wrong; Jhelum flows in the Kashmir Valley. 'Ravi' is wrong; Ravi barely touches J&K's southern border at Kathua.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText:
Given below are two statements, one labeled as Assertion (A) and the other as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): The Hokersar wetland near Srinagar is designated as a Ramsar site.
Reason (R): Hokersar serves as an important wintering ground for migratory birds from Central Asia and Siberia.

Choose the correct option:
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
questions.correctAnswer: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
questions.explanation: Hokersar is indeed a Ramsar site (A-correct) and its designation is precisely because of its ecological importance as a wintering ground for migratory birds (R-correct and explains A). Option 'R not the explanation' is wrong because the migratory bird habitat is the primary reason for Ramsar designation. Option 'A correct, R not correct' is wrong as R is factually accurate. Option 'A not correct' is wrong because Hokersar's Ramsar status is verified.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText: Which district of J&K is known as the 'Saffron Bowl of India'?
questions.explanation: Pulwama district, particularly the Pampore area, is known as the 'Saffron Bowl of India' due to extensive saffron cultivation. 'Srinagar' is wrong; while close to Pampore, the saffron fields are in Pulwama. 'Anantnag' is wrong; it is known for springs and temples. 'Budgam' is wrong; it is known for the airport and Yusmarg.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText:
Consider the following statements about the Amarnath Cave:

(i) It is located at an altitude of approximately 3,888 metres.
(ii) The naturally formed ice Shivalinga inside is worshipped by Hindu devotees.
(iii) The cave is located in the Lidder Valley of Anantnag district.
(iv) The annual yatra takes place during July-August (Shravan month).

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: All four statements are correct: the cave is at ~3,888m (i), contains a natural ice Shivalinga (ii), is in the Lidder Valley area of Anantnag (iii), and the yatra occurs in Shravan/July-August (iv). Option '(i), (ii) and (iv)' wrongly excludes (iii). Option '(i), (ii) and (iii)' wrongly excludes (iv). Option '(ii), (iii) and (iv)' wrongly excludes (i).

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText: The 'Chashme Shahi' Mughal garden in Srinagar literally means:
questions.explanation: Chashme Shahi means 'Royal Spring' — named after the natural spring within it. 'Garden of Joy' is wrong; that is the meaning of Nishat Bagh. 'Garden of Love' is wrong; that is the meaning of Shalimar Bagh. 'Abode of Spring' is wrong; it is a fabricated translation.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText:
Which of the following are centrally sponsored schemes actively implemented in J&K after 2019?

(i) Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana (PMAY)
(ii) Ayushman Bharat – SEHAT
(iii) PM-KISAN Samman Nidhi
(iv) Ujjwala Yojana

Select the correct combination:
questions.explanation: After J&K became a UT in 2019, all central schemes were extended, including PMAY (i), Ayushman Bharat-SEHAT (ii), PM-KISAN (iii), and Ujjwala (iv). Option '(i), (ii) and (iii) only' wrongly excludes Ujjwala. Option '(i), (iii) and (iv) only' wrongly excludes Ayushman Bharat. Option '(ii), (iii) and (iv) only' wrongly excludes PMAY.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText:
The following data shows the approximate installed capacity (in MW) of hydroelectric projects on selected rivers of J&K:

Chenab → Salal, Baglihar-I&II, Dulhasti, 1,860 MW
Jhelum → Uri-I, Uri-II, Lower Jhelum, 960 MW
Kishanganga → KHEP, 330 MW

What is the percentage share of Chenab-based projects in the total capacity shown above?
questions.explanation: Total = 1860 + 960 + 330 = 3150 MW. Chenab share = 1860/3150 × 100 ≈ 59%. 'Approximately 65%' is wrong (that would need ~2048 MW from Chenab). 'Approximately 50%' is wrong (that would need ~1575 MW). 'Approximately 72%' is wrong (that would need ~2268 MW).

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText: The Kokernag Spring, the largest freshwater spring in J&K, is located in which district?
questions.explanation: Kokernag Spring is located in the Anantnag district of Kashmir. 'Kulgam' is wrong; while close, Kokernag administratively falls in Anantnag. 'Pulwama' is wrong; it is farther north. 'Shopian' is wrong; it is in a different part of south Kashmir.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText:
Match the following festivals with their associated communities in J&K:

Column I:
(a) Navroz
(b) Lohri
(c) Hemis Festival
(d) Eid-ul-Fitr

Column II:
(i) Buddhist community
(ii) Dogra/Punjabi community in Jammu
(iii) Muslim community
(iv) Kashmiri Shia community

Choose the correct match:
questions.explanation: Navroz (Persian New Year) is celebrated by the Kashmiri Shia community (iv), Lohri by the Dogra/Punjabi community in Jammu (ii), Hemis Festival by the Buddhist community in Ladakh (i), and Eid-ul-Fitr by the Muslim community (iii). Option '(a)-(iii)...' wrongly assigns Navroz generically. Option '(a)-(iv), (b)-(i)...' wrongly assigns Lohri to Buddhists. Option '(a)-(i)...' wrongly assigns Navroz to Buddhists.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText: Under the J&K Reorganisation Act, 2019, how many seats are reserved for Scheduled Castes in the J&K Legislative Assembly?
questions.explanation: The Delimitation Commission reserved 7 seats for SCs in the 90-member J&K Legislative Assembly. '9' is wrong — that is the number of ST reserved seats. '4' is an arbitrary incorrect number. '11' exceeds the actual SC reservation.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText:
Consider the following statements about the climate of Ladakh:

(i) It has a cold desert climate with extreme temperature variations.
(ii) Annual rainfall is less than 100 mm in most parts.
(iii) It receives heavy snowfall from the southwest monsoon.
(iv) The Zanskar range acts as a rain shadow barrier.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: Ladakh has a cold desert climate (i-correct), receives very little rainfall (<100mm) (ii-correct), and the Zanskar range blocks moisture creating a rain shadow (iv-correct). Statement (iii) is wrong because Ladakh barely receives any southwest monsoon — the mountain barriers block it. Option '(i), (ii) and (iii)' wrongly includes (iii). Option '(i), (iii) and (iv)' wrongly includes (iii) and omits (ii). Option '(ii), (iii) and (iv)' wrongly includes (iii) and omits (i).

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText: The 'Dastangoi' tradition of J&K is related to:
options: The art of oral storytelling in Urdu/Persian
A traditional form of martial art
A method of wood carving unique to Kashmir
questions.correctAnswer: The art of oral storytelling in Urdu/Persian
questions.explanation: Dastangoi is the art of oral storytelling, narrating epic tales (dastans) in Urdu/Persian. 'Traditional martial art' is wrong; J&K does not have a well-known martial art by this name. 'Carpet weaving technique' is wrong; weaving techniques have different names. 'Wood carving method' is wrong; that is called Khatamband or walnut carving.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText:
Given below are two statements, one labeled as Assertion (A) and the other as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): The Jhelum river is prone to flooding in the Kashmir Valley.
Reason (R): The Jhelum has a very gentle gradient as it flows through the flat Kashmir Valley floor, making water drainage slow.

Choose the correct option:
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
questions.correctAnswer: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
questions.explanation: The Jhelum does flood frequently (e.g., 2014 floods) (A-correct), and the extremely gentle gradient across the flat valley floor causes slow drainage, directly leading to flooding (R-correct and explains A). Option 'R not the explanation' is wrong because the gradient issue is the primary hydrological cause. Option 'A correct, R not correct' is wrong because R accurately describes the river's behavior. Option 'A not correct' is wrong given the documented flood history.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText: The 'Sozni' embroidery of Kashmir is characterized by:
options: Fine needle-work on shawls using silk threads in floral patterns
Heavy gold-thread (zari) work on velvet fabric
Machine-made geometric patterns on cotton cloth
Appliqué patchwork using coloured felt pieces
questions.correctAnswer: Fine needle-work on shawls using silk threads in floral patterns
questions.explanation: Sozni (from the Persian word for needle) involves delicate hand-embroidery using silk threads in floral and paisley motifs on pashmina shawls. 'Gold-thread zari on velvet' is wrong; that describes Tilla work, not Sozni. 'Machine-made geometric on cotton' is wrong; Sozni is hand-crafted. 'Appliqué patchwork' is wrong; that describes Namda/Gabba crafts.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText:
Consider the following statements about the Panchayati Raj system in J&K:

(i) The 73rd Constitutional Amendment became applicable to J&K after 2019.
(ii) The three-tier panchayat system includes Halqa Panchayat, Block Development Council, and District Development Council.
(iii) DDC elections were first held in J&K in 2020.
(iv) The 73rd Amendment was applicable to J&K before 2019 as well.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: The 73rd Amendment became applicable after J&K became a UT in 2019 (i-correct), the three tiers are Halqa Panchayat, BDC, and DDC (ii-correct), and DDC elections were first held in December 2020 (iii-correct). Statement (iv) is wrong because the 73rd Amendment did NOT apply to J&K before 2019 due to its special status. Option '(i), (iii) and (iv)' wrongly includes (iv). Option '(ii), (iii) and (iv)' wrongly includes (iv) and omits (i). Option '(i), (ii) and (iv)' wrongly includes (iv) and omits (iii).

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText: Fill in the blank: The __________ is the only inland waterway (national waterway) declared in J&K, running through the Jhelum River and Dal Lake system.
questions.explanation: National Waterway 49, declared under the National Waterways Act 2016, covers the Jhelum River from Wular Lake to Khannabal including Dal and Anchar lakes. 'NW 25' is wrong; it is in another state. 'NW 3' is wrong; it refers to the West Coast Canal in Kerala. 'NW 71' is wrong; no such waterway exists in J&K.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText: The 'Khatamband' craft of Kashmir involves:
options: Geometrical ceiling work using interlocking wooden pieces without nails
Chain-stitch embroidery using an Aari needle
Copper engraving on utensils and samovars
questions.correctAnswer: Geometrical ceiling work using interlocking wooden pieces without nails
questions.explanation: Khatamband is the traditional Kashmiri art of creating intricately patterned wooden ceilings using interlocking pieces fitted without nails. 'Paper-maché items' is wrong; that is a separate craft. 'Chain-stitch embroidery' is wrong; that is Aari work. 'Copper engraving' is wrong; that is called Naqqashi on copper.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText:
Given below are two statements, one labeled as Assertion (A) and the other as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): Ladakh was separated from J&K and made a Union Territory without a legislature.
Reason (R): The people of Ladakh had long demanded UT status to ensure focused development separate from Kashmir-centric governance.

Choose the correct option:
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
questions.correctAnswer: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
questions.explanation: Ladakh was indeed made a separate UT without legislature under the 2019 Reorganisation Act (A-correct), and the demand for UT status from Ladakh's people citing neglect under Kashmir-focused governance was a key reason (R-correct and explains A). Option 'R not the explanation' is wrong because the demand directly influenced the decision. Option 'A correct, R not correct' is wrong because the demand is well-documented. Option 'A not correct' is wrong because Ladakh is indeed a UT without legislature.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText: The 'Bakerwal' community of J&K is primarily known for:
options: Nomadic pastoralism — rearing goats and sheep in high-altitude pastures
Traditional carpet weaving in the Kashmir Valley
Fishing and houseboat operations on Dal Lake
Rice cultivation in the R.S. Pura belt of Jammu
questions.correctAnswer: Nomadic pastoralism — rearing goats and sheep in high-altitude pastures
questions.explanation: Bakerwal (also Bakerwals) are a nomadic pastoral community who migrate seasonally with their livestock (goats, sheep, horses) between low-altitude winter pastures and high-altitude summer meadows. 'Carpet weaving' is wrong; that is associated with settled artisans. 'Fishing and houseboats' is wrong; that is associated with the Hanjis. 'Rice cultivation' is wrong; they are nomadic, not settled agriculturists.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText:
Match the following government institutions in J&K with their locations:

Column I:
(a) IIT Jammu
(b) NIT Srinagar
(c) AIIMS Jammu
(d) IIM Jammu

Column II:
(i) Vijaypur (Samba)
(ii) Nagrota (Jammu)
(iii) Hazratbal (Srinagar)
(iv) Jagti (Jammu)

Choose the correct match:
questions.explanation: IIT Jammu's permanent campus is at Jagti (iv), NIT Srinagar is at Hazratbal (iii), AIIMS Jammu is being built at Vijaypur in Samba (i), and IIM Jammu campus is at Nagrota (ii). Option '(a)-(ii)...' wrongly places IIT at Nagrota. Option '(a)-(iv), (b)-(i)...' wrongly places NIT at Samba. Option '(a)-(i)...' wrongly places IIT at Vijaypur.

questions.questionText: The total number of assembly constituencies in the Union Territory of J&K after the 2022 delimitation is:
questions.explanation: The Delimitation Commission finalized 90 assembly constituencies for J&K (43 in Jammu and 47 in Kashmir). '87' is the previous count before delimitation. '83' is an older figure. '95' exceeds the actual number decided.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText:
Consider the following statements about the Chenab Railway Bridge (Anji Khad):

(i) It is part of the Udhampur-Srinagar-Baramulla Rail Link (USBRL) project.
(ii) It is the world's highest railway arch bridge.
(iii) It spans the Anji Khad gorge in the Reasi district.
(iv) It is higher than the Eiffel Tower.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: All four are correct: it is part of USBRL (i), is the world's highest railway bridge (ii), spans Anji Khad gorge in Reasi (iii), and at 359m is taller than the Eiffel Tower's 330m (iv). Option '(i), (ii) and (iii) only' wrongly excludes (iv). Option '(i), (iii) and (iv) only' wrongly excludes (ii). Option '(i), (ii) and (iv) only' wrongly excludes (iii).

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText:
The following data shows the number of tourists (in lakhs) visiting J&K over four years:

2021 → 72
2022 → 168
2023 → 210
2024 → 235

In which year was the absolute increase in tourist arrivals over the previous year the highest?
questions.explanation: Increase in 2022 = 168 − 72 = 96 lakhs. Increase in 2023 = 210 − 168 = 42 lakhs. Increase in 2024 = 235 − 210 = 25 lakhs. So 2022 had the highest absolute increase (96 lakhs). '2023' is wrong (increase was 42). '2024' is wrong (increase was 25). '2022 and 2023 equal' is wrong (96 ≠ 42).

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText: The 'Peer Ki Gali' on the Mughal Road is significant because:
options: It is the highest point on the Mughal Road at about 3,490 metres
It houses the largest Buddhist monastery in J&K
It is the source of the Chenab River
It marks the border between J&K and Himachal Pradesh
questions.correctAnswer: It is the highest point on the Mughal Road at about 3,490 metres
questions.explanation: Peer Ki Gali is the highest point on the Mughal Road at approximately 3,490m on the Pir Panjal range. 'Largest Buddhist monastery' is wrong; monasteries are in Ladakh. 'Source of Chenab' is wrong; Chenab originates from confluence of Chandra and Bhaga in HP. 'Border between J&K and HP' is wrong; the Mughal Road is entirely within J&K.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText:
Consider the following statements about the 'One District One Product' (ODOP) initiative in J&K:

(i) Pulwama has been identified for saffron under this scheme.
(ii) Kupwara has been identified for walnuts.
(iii) Srinagar has been identified for Paper Machie crafts.
(iv) Kathua has been identified for apple production.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: Pulwama is identified for saffron (i-correct), Kupwara for walnuts (ii-correct), and Srinagar for Paper Machie (iii-correct). Kathua is NOT identified for apple — apple is associated with districts like Shopian/Baramulla; Kathua is known for Basmati rice (iv-wrong). Option '(i), (ii) and (iv)' wrongly includes (iv). Option '(i), (iii) and (iv)' wrongly includes (iv) and omits (ii). Option '(ii), (iii) and (iv)' wrongly includes (iv) and omits (i).

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText:
The following data shows the area (in hectares) under major horticultural crops in J&K:

Apple → 1,65,000
Walnut → 90,000
Almond → 18,000
Saffron → 3,715

What is the approximate percentage of area under walnut to the total horticultural area shown?
questions.explanation: Total = 1,65,000 + 90,000 + 18,000 + 3,715 = 2,76,715 hectares. Walnut share = 90,000/2,76,715 × 100 ≈ 32.5% ≈ 33%. 'Approximately 40%' is wrong (that would need ~1,10,000 hectares). 'Approximately 25%' is wrong (too low). 'Approximately 45%' is wrong (too high).

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText: The Sufi shrine of Charar-i-Sharief in Budgam district is dedicated to which saint?
questions.explanation: The Charar-i-Sharief shrine in Budgam houses the tomb of Sheikh Noor-ud-din Noorani (also called Nund Rishi), the patron saint of Kashmir. 'Shah-e-Hamadan' is wrong; his shrine is Khanqah-e-Moula in Srinagar. 'Bulbul Shah' is wrong; his shrine is in Srinagar. 'Bahauddin Zakariya' is wrong; he is associated with Multan in Pakistan.
